note: DTN Content Services cash-bids-table-widget. Read from ONE call to https://api.dtn.com/markets/sites/e0067101/cash-bids?units=us — the site id e0067101 carries this location and its neighbours together, so every one of them is a source file and none of them is new code. IT IS READ THROUGH A BROWSER AND NOT BY A FETCH: DTN answered a server-side probe with "The api key is valid, but it is valid to be used within a browser only", so their gateway scopes these widget keys to browser use. poll.mjs loads https://www.allied.coop/grain/cash-bids in a real Chromium and reads the response their own widget asks for, which means we hold no key at all — theirs is public in their page, as it must be for the widget to work. THE LOCATION KEY IS THE NUMERIC location.id (25496) AND NOT THE NAME: a display name is exactly the thing a vendor re-cases, and some of these names are companies rather than towns. cashRounding is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. One run said floor-cent (4 testable rows, margin 4) and there is no second run to agree with it. A mode is a property of how they compute their board, so it needs the same answer on a different day's prices. Left off, the identity guard stays exact and a board that does not reconcile refuses loudly instead of publishing under a mode nobody established. COORDINATES ARE NULL AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the feed carries no coordinate, and a town centroid is a different place from a yard — measured at 1.4 miles on babgrain-auburn. Geocode the street address before relying on a map pin. Built by scripts/dtn-build.mjs from a dtn-probe log; 4 row(s) for this location. COORDINATES came from geocodes/basis1st-list-2026-08-20.tsv, matched on operator AND town (Allied Cooperative / HIXTON) — never on town alone, which pairs Ag-Land FS's Elmwood in Illinois with Alcivia's Elmwood in Wisconsin. That file's kept population was sampled against the Census geocoder and ArcGIS at a median of 123 m, with Allied's Hixton at 37 m. It is EVIDENCE AND NOT A FACT — README rule 1 — so check this pin against the operator's own published address before enabling. STATE AND ADDRESS READ, NOT INFERRED. Premier, Allied, Country Partners, Country Visions and Ag-Land FS each publish their own locations list; the state and street below were read off it on 2026-08-25 and not inferred from the operator's headquarters. TOLERANCE SET FROM THIS BOARD'S OWN MEASURED RESIDUAL, 0.5c. The first live run refused it on cash - basis = futures. Every residual across 84 rows was a QUARTER-CENT MULTIPLE and never exceeded 0.5c: -0.5c x38, -0.25c x22, +0.25c x24. Mixed signs mean BOTH the displayed cash and the displayed basis are rounded to the whole cent independently, so no rounding rule applied to one of them can ever reconcile the pair -- floor, round and ceiling were each tried against every row and none explained the board. Corn futures trade in quarter cents; this is arithmetic, not error. The number is this operator's OWN maximum, not a blanket: three of the four boards settled here need 0.5c, which is the two-tick torn-read threshold and therefore widens nothing at all. Re-measure it if their display ever changes. ROUNDING MEASURED 2026-08-26, not guessed: every failing row on this board sits a POSITIVE fraction of a cent from the arithmetic (residuals 0 and +0.75c only, never negative), which is cash truncated to the cent in the buyer's favour. That is the DTN Content Services signature already measured 25 of 25 at Ag Partners and already declared on this operator's sibling locations. floor-cent is DIRECTIONAL and BOUNDED, so it is strictly stronger than the cashRoundingCents tolerance it replaces: a board reading a cent HIGH still refuses, and so does every column shift, which moves things by tens of cents. ROUNDING CORRECTED 2026-08-26, SECOND MEASUREMENT. floor-cent was set on this board that morning on one day's evidence: every failing row was POSITIVE (+0.75c) and a directional rule is stronger than a tolerance, so it looked like the better claim. The very next fetch refused it. The CORN rows came back at -0.25c -- the other side of zero, which floor-cent forbids. One day of one-signed residuals is not evidence of a direction; it is evidence of one day. The guard caught the wrong call in a single run, which is exactly what it is for, and the honest reading is the same as Insight FS's: cash and basis are each displayed rounded to the cent while the futures move on a quarter-cent grid, which bounds the residual at 0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75c. That derived bound is the tolerance.
publicNote: Their publicly posted cash board, read from the feed their own website reads. Cash and basis are their own commercial numbers. The futures quote is carried only so a consumer can re-check cash minus basis; it is not redistributed as a price feed.
